items.summary: Start replacement search at the right time
items.description:
Let an employee establish their vehicle preferences when they receive their current car, then use available mileage and contract timing to identify an appropriate replacement-search window. Help them plan before a vehicle release or offer email while retaining their control over Buddy engagement and any order.

Agree the permitted inputs and employee permission, and the meaning of the replacement window. Reuse the saved brief, current-car and renewal contracts; predictive timing is the additional capability.

Overlap: FUCQ-86 already saves preferences and engages Buddy; FUCQ-110 covers renewal help and lifecycle; FUCQ-338 covers a specific current-car configuration and supported history. None of these references is an automatic dependency or expanded acceptance contract.

items.summary: Offer earlier replacement when a current car is wanted for resale
items.description:
When young-used-car demand favours an employee's current vehicle or specification, identify a suitable earlier replacement opportunity and invite the employee to change voluntarily.

Keep this distinct from normal renewal. The opportunity depends on scheme authority, suitable replacement supply and a worthwhile commercial outcome; the feedback does not authorise automatic contract shortening or vehicle return.

Overlap: FUCQ-110 supplies replacement handover and old-car return planning; FUCQ-74 supplies future scheme-order planning. The used-market-triggered early replacement opportunity is additional intent.

items.summary: Plan scheme orders against used-market and employee demand
items.description:
Make future used-market demand an explicit input to scheme model, specification and return-timing decisions alongside employee preferences. Help the scheme team understand the trade-off between suitable employee choices and the vehicles future used-car customers want to buy.

Establish the actual market inputs and business objectives and show how they change the planning decision. Preserve employee suitability. A presenter's provisional option-desirability weights are not verified market valuations.

Overlap: FUCQ-74 already covers learned employee demand, constrained quantities, stock/inbound supply, business objectives and intentional submission; FUCQ-90 covers demand/outcome visibility and order tracking; FUCQ-337 covers meaningful exact-option comparisons. This item captures the remaining used-market input and objective capability, reusing that work without duplicating the dashboard or rewriting its claimed acceptance. Prior discussion is in docs/gcsp/business-model-exploration.md.

items.summary: Compare estimated fuel and energy running costs
items.description:
Help an employee understand what an offered car might cost in fuel or electricity, alongside their current car where supported, using mileage, consumption and dated fuel/charging-price assumptions. Make the estimate, units and basis understandable.

Reuse the available vehicle facts and current-versus-offered comparison. An economy preference or consumption figure alone is not a monetary running-cost estimate. The requested capability does not include tax, finance, insurance or a complete total-cost-of-ownership calculator.

Overlap: FUCQ-337 supplies meaningful exact-configuration comparison and FUCQ-338 supplies current-car context. Existing fuel-economy preferences remain useful inputs rather than a substitute for this estimate.

items.summary: Refine fair access and acceptable-offer policy
items.description:
Refine the existing fair-access and offer-suitability proposals using feedback from manufacturing and shift employees who cannot join the release-time rush. Preserve the aim of being at least as satisfied with the car obtained, with less employee effort.

Reconcile docs/gcsp/buddy-release-fairness-review-2026-11-11.md and docs/gcsp/paula-touring-match-diagnosis-2026-11-11.md before choosing a rule. Agree the treatment of competition misses, renewal urgency, rejection, manual access and acceptable preference fit. Distinguish allocation priority from minimum acceptable fit, and test the proposed experience with representative employees and ordering stakeholders.

The current recorded rule is renewal date, then fit, then a seeded tie-break. The narrated queue adjustments, penalties, thresholds and guarantees are proposals, not adopted BMW policy or unmet existing acceptance criteria. Backlog capture does not implement or adopt a particular lottery, rejection penalty, minimum score, extra hold or automatic priority guarantee. A two-hour response window is not proven to meet every shift-worker need.

Overlap: FUCQ-87 covers scarce-stock allocation and holds; FUCQ-86/88/89 cover delegation, notification and decisions; FUCQ-132 compares routes. Carry forward the existing proposals rather than creating another basic Buddy implementation.
